title: spec review: Q4 v2: orchestrator/planner_router.py — Planner tier router: modes off|shadow|active, hard vs soft Fable escalation, evidence gate, Fable reserve, hold instead of silent downgrade; decision_log kind planner_route (P5, P9, P11, P17, P18)
spec:
Why: decision.route (orchestrator/decision.py) decides routine/investigate/escalate and names escalate_tier fable; planner_runs.launch_routed (lines 1090-1110) resolves that alias to [models].planner. There is no Opus tier between investigate (sonnet) and escalate (fable), no hard/soft split, no evidence gate, no Fable reserve and no hold path (brief P5, P9, P11, P17, P18). Spec review T-0681's five risks are folded in: plain notify, record() inputs, dict access, classification producer, evidence provenance.
What: new pure module orchestrator/planner_router.py plus one new entry "planner_route" in decision_log.KINDS. No bus, pool or file reads; inputs never mutated. Every structured input is a plain dict read with .get(): ctx (decision.route's ctx, see decision.py docstring), classification (planner_taxonomy.classify output, module orchestrator/planner_taxonomy.py from T-0675 on goal/T-0674: keys decision_type, architectural, ambiguous, risk_class none|low|high, signals, band, task_class), evidence ({"n": int, "noninferior": True|False|None, "reescalation_rate": float}; produced later by Q5 planner_scorecard.class_evidence, same goal; this module only consumes the dict), availability ({tier: {"available": bool, "reason": str}, "fable_reserve_ok": bool}), jev_signal ({"soft_adjust": float} or None). route is decision.Route (attributes name, reason, evidence, tier) or a dict with the same keys; accept both via a tiny _get(obj, key) helper.
- load_cfg(pool_cfg) -> routing dict with defaults from pool_cfg.get("planner", {}).get("routing", {}): mode "shadow" (off|shadow|active), default_tier "opus", escalation_tier "fable", hard_complexity_min 9, hard_security True, hard_spec_review_request_changes_min 2, hard_ambiguous True, min_samples 20, shadow_sample_rate 1.0, fable_reserve_share 0.2, jev_mode "shadow", soft_threshold 0.5. An unknown mode or a non-numeric number -> default plus one plain notify.notify(f"pool.toml [planner.routing].{key} invalid ({value!r}); using {default!r}") per key per process (module-level set of warned keys), exactly like daemon._load_scheduler_cfg; never raises, never touches the bus.
- @dataclass(frozen=True) RouterDecision: tier (str), mode (str), hard (bool), hold (bool), hold_reason (str|None), reasons (tuple[str, ...]), soft_score (float), shadow_tier (str|None), candidates (tuple[str, ...]), evidence (dict), decision_type (str), hard_reasons (tuple[str, ...]).
- hard_escalation(classification, ctx, route, cfg) -> list[str]: route name != "escalate" -> []; route reason startswith "unknown:" or reason == "routes_disabled" -> "unknown_risk"; complexity (ctx.get("complexity") or classification band 7-10 with ctx complexity unknown counts as 0) >= hard_complexity_min -> "complexity"; hard_security and (classification.get("risk_class") == "high" or ctx.get("security_trigger") or ctx.get("touches_auth") or ctx.get("touches_data_deletion")) -> "security"; hard_ambiguous and classification.get("decision_type") in ("architectural_replan", "ambiguous_requirement") -> "architectural_or_ambiguous"; ctx.get("spec_review_request_changes", 0) >= hard_spec_review_request_changes_min -> "repeated_spec_rejection"; both ctx auto_fix_rounds_used and auto_fix_rounds ints and used >= cap -> "lineage_cap"; ctx.get("reescalation") -> "reescalation". Callers pass ctx["complexity"] (task complexity for held, goal complexity otherwise); document this.
- soft_score(classification, ctx, evidence, jev_signal=None) -> float in [0, 1]: +0.3 classification architectural; +0.2 ctx complexity in (7, 8); +0.2 evidence reescalation_rate > 0.2; +0.2 evidence noninferior is False; +0.1 risk_class low; plus jev_signal soft_adjust clamped to [-0.2, 0.2]; clamp to [0, 1]. Tokens/usd never inputs (docstring).
- decide(classification, ctx, route, *, cfg, availability, evidence, jev_signal=None, sample=1.0) -> RouterDecision. Rules in order: route name != "escalate" -> tier = route tier or "fable", reasons ("not_escalate_route",), unchanged in every mode. mode off -> tier route tier or "fable", reasons ("mode_off",), shadow_tier None. hard reasons non-empty -> tier escalation_tier, hard True; escalation tier unavailable -> hold True, hold_reason f"fable_unavailable:{reason}" (never downgrade, jev ignored). mode shadow -> tier escalation_tier (production unchanged); shadow_tier = default_tier when not hard and default tier available and sample <= shadow_sample_rate, else None with a reason (shadow_hard|shadow_default_unavailable|sampled_out). mode active, not hard: default_tier when evidence noninferior is True and n >= min_samples and soft_score < soft_threshold ("evidence_noninferior"); elif fable_reserve_ok is False and noninferior is not False -> default_tier ("fable_reserve_low"); else escalation_tier ("insufficient_evidence" when noninferior is None or n < min_samples, "soft_escalation" otherwise); a chosen tier that is unavailable falls back to the other available tier for soft decisions ("fallback:<tier>_unavailable"); none available -> hold, hold_reason "no_planner_tier_available".
- record(decision, *, subject, route, jev_signal=None, root=None) -> decision_log.record(kind="planner_route", subject=goal id, candidates=list(decision.candidates), hard_constraints=list(decision.hard_reasons), deterministic={"route": route name, "reason": route reason}, historical=decision.evidence, jev=jev_signal, selected=decision.tier if not decision.hold else "hold", reason=";".join(decision.reasons), mode=decision.mode, extra={"decision_type", "hold_reason", "shadow_tier", "soft_score"}, root=root).
- explain(decision) -> one line. decision_log.py change: append "planner_route" to KINDS only.
acceptance: tests/test_planner_router.py::test_mode_off_reproduces_route_tier — mode off returns the route tier (fable) with reasons mode_off, shadow_tier None, hold False for every decision type; a non-escalate route returns its own tier unchanged in every mode

tests/test_planner_router.py::test_hard_escalation_never_downgrades_and_holds_when_fable_unavailable — complexity 9, security, ambiguous_requirement and repeated_spec_rejection each yield tier fable hard True in active mode even with noninferior evidence and jev soft_adjust -0.2; with fable unavailable the decision is hold True with hold_reason starting fable_unavailable

tests/test_planner_router.py::test_shadow_mode_keeps_fable_and_sets_shadow_tier — shadow mode yields tier fable and shadow_tier opus for a soft decision, shadow_tier None for a hard decision, when opus is unavailable, or when sample exceeds shadow_sample_rate

tests/test_planner_router.py::test_active_mode_requires_evidence_and_ignores_tokens — active with n 25 noninferior True picks opus; n 5 picks fable with reason insufficient_evidence; noninferior False picks fable; evidence carrying tokens_saved 1e9 changes nothing; fable_reserve_ok False with noninferior None picks opus with reason fable_reserve_low

tests/test_planner_router.py::test_load_cfg_defaults_and_record_kind — missing table gives every documented default; an invalid mode falls back to shadow with exactly one notify.notify call and no bus access; record(decision, subject, route, jev_signal) appends a decision_log row of kind planner_route with deterministic.route and jev set, readable by decision_log.explain under a sandbox root

risks.issue: record()'s extra argument is written as a set literal `extra={"decision_type", "hold_reason", "shadow_tier", "soft_score"}` instead of a dict mapping those keys to decision.<attr> values. Implemented literally, `extra` is a python set; decision_log.record stores it verbatim and schedlog.append (orchestrator/schedlog.py:15) calls json.dumps(record), which raises TypeError on a set. record() would crash, taking down test_load_cfg_defaults_and_record_kind with it.

hard_escalation's complexity rule falls back to 'classification band 7-10' when ctx has no complexity, but attribution.band (orchestrator/attribution.py:118-125) returns a string like "7-10"/"4-6"/"1-3"/unknown, not a number -- it cannot be compared with `>= hard_complexity_min` as written. No acceptance test exercises the missing-ctx-complexity path, so whatever ad-hoc numeric mapping an implementer picks (e.g. treating band "7-10" as satisfying any hard_complexity_min, even 9 or 10) goes unverified and could hard-escalate complexity-7/8 goals that should route through soft scoring.

RouterDecision.candidates is declared but decide() never specifies how it's populated, and no acceptance test inspects decision.candidates or record()'s resulting row['candidates']/row['rejected']. decision_log's whole audit purpose (candidates considered vs rejected) can silently degenerate to an always-empty tuple without any test catching it.

In the hard-escalation branch, decide() defines hard_reasons via hard_escalation() but never states what the separate `reasons` field should hold for that branch (RouterDecision has both). Left to the implementer's guess; no acceptance test pins reasons vs hard_reasons equivalence in the hard case.

load_cfg() defines defaults for fable_reserve_share and jev_mode, but neither key is read anywhere in the specified hard_escalation/soft_score/decide algorithm (decide consumes availability.fable_reserve_ok and jev_signal directly, both external inputs). Documenting unused config knobs under this module misleads whoever edits pool.toml later into thinking planner_router.py acts on them.

Spec says the per-key notify dedup works 'exactly like daemon._load_scheduler_cfg', but that function (orchestrator/daemon.py:593-596) uses one dedicated module-level bool per named warning, not a generic set keyed by arbitrary config key. The cited precedent doesn't match the 'set of warned keys' mechanism the spec actually asks for.

suggested_spec_changes: Rewrite the extra= construction as a dict: extra={"decision_type": decision.decision_type, "hold_reason": decision.hold_reason, "shadow_tier": decision.shadow_tier, "soft_score": decision.soft_score}.

Replace the band-based complexity fallback with an explicit numeric mapping (e.g. a BAND_FLOOR = {"1-3": 1, "4-6": 4, "7-10": 7, None: 0, "unknown": 0} lookup) and add an acceptance case where ctx has no 'complexity' key and classification band is "7-10", asserting the exact resulting hard/soft outcome.

Add one sentence defining RouterDecision.candidates content (e.g. candidates = (default_tier, escalation_tier) always) and one acceptance assertion on decision.candidates / the recorded row's candidates and rejected fields.
State explicitly that reasons == hard_reasons in the hard-escalation branch (or define the divergence) so RouterDecision's two reason fields aren't left to implementer discretion.

Either wire fable_reserve_share and jev_mode into this module's logic or drop them from planner_router.load_cfg's defaults and document which module (presumably the one producing `availability`) owns them.
